EasyCart E-Commerce System

A practical start-to-finish guide for running the public web shop and the administration application. Screen examples use demo data; your products, company name, currency, permissions and translations may differ.

Open storefront guideOpen admin guide

1. System overview

The project has three applications that work together.

Backend API

ASP.NET Core API connected to SQL Server. It stores company settings, products, stock, operations, customers and orders.

ASP.NET CoreEF CoreSQL Server

Admin application

Used by authorized staff to manage products, inventory, purchases, manual sales, orders, customers, reports, users and settings.

ReactPermissions

Web storefront

Used by customers to browse products, manage wishlist/cart, verify an account, checkout and track orders.

ResponsivePWA
The system is configured for one company with optional branches. The company profile, currency, branches and storefront content are managed from the admin application.

2. Start the system locally

2.1 Prerequisites

  • .NET SDK compatible with the backend project
  • SQL Server and a valid connection string
  • Node.js and npm
  • Modern browser such as Chrome or Edge

2.2 Configure backend

1
Open the backend settings.

Set ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection for your SQL Server. Use environment variables or user secrets for passwords, JWT keys, email credentials and verification hash keys.

2
Set the first administrator.

Configure SeedAdmin__Email and SeedAdmin__Password securely before the first run when a new admin must be seeded.

3
Run the API.
cd backend
dotnet restore
dotnet run

The default development HTTP address is http://localhost:5188.

2.3 Configure and run both React applications

# Storefront
cd frontend/web
# Create .env.local
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5188/api
npm install
npm run dev

# Admin (in another terminal)
cd frontend/admin
# Set VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5188/api when needed
npm install
npm run dev
Use the exact URLs printed by Vite. When both React apps run at the same time, Vite may choose different ports automatically.

4. Storefront home page

The home page introduces the company, promotes categories and displays compact featured and new-arrival product cards.

Demo home screen showing the upgraded realistic category cards and compact five-column product layout.

What customers can do

Use the main navigation

Open Home, Shop, Categories, Deals or Track Order. The header also provides search, wishlist, cart and account actions.

Browse responsive products

Featured Products and New Arrivals adapt across devices: one compact horizontal card on phones, then 2, 3, 4 and 5 columns on larger screens.

Browse categories

Each category card shows a strong product image, category name, product count and child-category hints. Select a card to open the catalog filtered to that category.

5. Browse and filter products

Catalog with category shortcuts, filters, search and product cards.
1
Open Shop.

Select Shop in the header or use View All from a home section.

2
Search.

Enter a product name, brand, category or barcode and select Search.

3
Filter.

Use category, brand, unit, price range, stock status and Featured filters. On mobile, filters open in a dialog.

4
Sort and paginate.

Choose the desired sort order and use pagination when more products are available.

The catalog product-card design remains unchanged by the home-page compact-card update, so product browsing retains its existing comfortable card size.

6. Product details

Product image gallery, availability, pricing, quantity and Add to Cart.
  • Review product images, category, strength, description, rating and stock status.
  • Check current price, old price and discount where available.
  • Select the correct unit or conversion when the product supports multiple units.
  • Choose a quantity within the configured minimum, maximum and stock limits.
  • Select Add to Cart or use the wishlist action for later.
  • Review product ratings and customer reviews below the main product section.

7. Wishlist, cart and checkout

Cart item management, delivery information, payment method and order summary.

Cart workflow

1
Add products.

Use the bag button on a card or Add to Cart on the product page.

2
Review quantities.

Increase, decrease or remove items. The system recalculates subtotal, shipping and total.

3
Continue to checkout.

Sign in when required. At least one account contact—email or phone—must be confirmed before an order can be placed.

4
Complete delivery details.

Enter the customer name, confirmed contact, address and optional note. Choose cash or bank transfer when enabled.

5
Place the order.

For bank transfer, enter the transaction/reference number. Save the generated order number.

8. Customer account and order tracking

Verified contact, order history and guest tracking flow.

Account

The account page displays customer type, phone, order count, contact verification and order history. A development-only verification code may be returned locally when a delivery provider is completely unconfigured; production never returns codes.

Track an order

1
Open Track Order.

Enter the complete order number and the phone used at checkout.

2
Select Track.

The page displays order, payment and fulfillment status plus the event timeline.

9. Admin sign-in

Administration login screen.
1
Open the admin URL.

Use the address printed by the admin Vite server or your deployed admin site.

2
Enter authorized credentials.

The login endpoint creates an access token. The application automatically signs the user out when the token is invalid or expired.

3
Confirm navigation visibility.

Menu items are permission-controlled. Missing items normally mean that the current role does not have the required permission.

10. Admin dashboard

Key performance indicators, revenue trend, stock alerts and recent orders.

Use the dashboard at the start of the day to identify urgent work.

  • Review today’s revenue and order volume.
  • Open orders that are awaiting confirmation or fulfillment.
  • Investigate low-stock, out-of-stock and expiring products.
  • Check recent customer and sales activity.
  • Refresh when you need the newest values.

11. Company and storefront setup

Company Settings

Configure company name, logo, contact information, address, currency, bank-transfer details, branches, operation limits and expiry-alert periods.

General Types

Create and maintain categories, brands, units, customer types, expense types and other lookup values used by the product and operation forms.

Storefront Content

Manage home hero eyebrow, title, description, primary/secondary buttons, hero image and translations without rebuilding the frontend.

Complete company, branch, currency and lookup setup before creating products. This keeps pricing, inventory and reports consistent.

12. Product management

Product list and inventory summary with demo data.

Create one product

1
Open Products → New product.

Enter product name, barcode, strength, descriptions and optional slug.

2
Select classification.

Choose category, brand and base unit from configured lookup values.

3
Configure pricing.

Set the default price and optional customer-type prices, old prices, date ranges and unit-conversion overrides.

4
Configure stock presentation.

Set reorder point and optional display stock. Display stock changes what customers see; real stock remains controlled by inventory.

5
Add images and status.

Choose a primary image, gallery images, Featured and Active state, then save.

Bulk work

Use Bulk Create to add many products. On the product list, select multiple rows to bulk update or delete. Search, filters, pagination and PDF export help manage large catalogs.

13. Inventory management

The Inventory page has overview and transaction views.

  • Filter products by healthy, low-stock or out-of-stock status.
  • Review on-hand, reserved and available quantities.
  • Open stock lots to view lot number, cost, manufacturing and expiry dates.
  • Record allowed inventory movements and adjustments with a clear reference.
  • Monitor reorder point and expiry alerts.
  • Do not edit stock only to make storefront numbers look better; use display stock for that purpose.
Every stock-changing operation should have a source document or clear reason. This protects the audit trail and financial accuracy.

14. Business operations

Purchases

Record supplier purchases, product lines, quantities, unit cost, lots, expiry dates and settlements. Confirming purchases increases stock and affects payable/financial records.

Manual sales

Create counter or direct sales that do not originate from the storefront. Select customer when needed, add lines, receive payment and complete the sale.

Staff

Maintain staff records used by company operations where enabled.

Expenses

Record operating expenses using configured expense types, dates, references, notes and amounts.

Safe operation sequence

Create the document → verify lines and totals → verify settlement/payment → save or confirm → check resulting stock and ledger impact.

15. Online orders

Order queue beside customer records.
1
Open Orders.

Use filters and pagination to find pending, processing, confirmed, fulfilled, delivered or cancelled orders.

2
Open order details.

Review customer, address, contact verification, products, quantities, pricing, totals, payment method and reference.

3
Move through the workflow.

Follow the available actions in order: review, confirm payment/order, prepare, fulfill/dispatch and deliver. Available actions depend on current status and permission.

4
Handle cancellation carefully.

Confirm whether reserved stock and payment records need reversal. Add a meaningful reason where supported.

16. Customers, pricing and reviews

Customers

Customers are created automatically during checkout and can also be added manually. Open a customer to review contact details, orders, financial activity and customer-specific context.

Customer-type pricing

A product can have different active prices for customer types. The storefront resolves the appropriate price after the customer is identified.

Reviews

Use the Reviews page to review product feedback and apply the available moderation workflow.

17. Financial reports and exports

Financial performance, exports, company profile and storefront settings.

Use Financial Reports to review revenue, purchases, expenses, gross profit and other available summaries. Apply date and business filters before exporting.

  • Confirm the date range and currency.
  • Check whether only finalized/paid documents should be included.
  • Export Excel for analysis and PDF for sharing or printing.
  • Compare report totals with source orders, sales, purchases and expenses when investigating a difference.

18. Users, roles, trash and audit

Users

Create administrator/staff users, update profile information and assign roles according to job responsibility.

Roles

Grant the minimum permissions necessary. Test a role with a non-admin account before using it in production.

Trash

Use Trash for supported soft-deleted company records. Restore only after confirming that the record will not conflict with an active replacement.

Audit

Audit logs help answer who changed what and when. Use them during troubleshooting, stock reconciliation and security review.

19. Recommended daily checklist

Opening

  • Check backend and both frontends are available.
  • Review failed notifications or sync issues.
  • Check pending orders and payment references.
  • Review low-stock and expiry alerts.

During the day

  • Record purchases, sales and expenses promptly.
  • Keep order statuses current.
  • Use clear references and notes.
  • Verify customer details before delivery.

Closing

  • Review today’s sales and payments.
  • Investigate negative or unexpected stock.
  • Confirm unresolved orders.
  • Export or review financial summaries when required.

Weekly

  • Review permissions and inactive users.
  • Check database backups.
  • Review audit activity and deleted records.
  • Test restoring a backup in a safe environment.

20. Troubleshooting

ProblemCheckResolution
Frontend cannot load dataAPI URL, backend status, browser Network tab, CORSConfirm VITE_API_BASE_URL ends with /api and the API is reachable.
Admin menu item missingCurrent user role and permissionsAssign the required permission and sign in again.
Images do not displayStored URL, API origin, uploaded file and static file hostingConfirm the backend serves the image path and HTTPS origins are consistent.
Checkout blockedAuthentication, confirmed contact, stock and required delivery fieldsVerify email/phone and correct invalid cart or address data.
Stock does not matchLots, reservations, purchases, sales, cancellations and adjustmentsUse inventory transactions and audit logs; do not directly patch quantities in SQL.
Email/SMS verification failsProvider configuration, credentials, hash key, timeout and logsConfigure providers through secure environment variables and test delivery.
Build install failsnpm registry, lockfile, Node version and networkUse an accessible registry/cache and run npm ci when a valid lockfile is available.

21. Security and backup rules

Never commit real passwords, app passwords, JWT signing keys, verification hash keys or bearer tokens. Store them in environment variables, .NET user secrets, IIS settings or a production secret manager. Rotate any secret that was previously committed or shared.
  • Use HTTPS for API, admin and storefront in production.
  • Use a strong unique JWT key and verification hash key.
  • Protect SQL Server and restrict database accounts.
  • Back up the database before migrations and major configuration changes.
  • Keep uploaded product/company images in the backup plan.
  • Apply least-privilege roles and remove inactive accounts.
  • Review logs without exposing customer or credential data.

22. Quick glossary

TermMeaning
On handTotal physical stock recorded by the system.
ReservedStock held for orders or operations but not yet completed.
AvailableOn-hand quantity minus reserved quantity.
Reorder pointQuantity at which staff should consider purchasing more stock.
Inventory lotA batch of a product with its own cost, lot number and expiry information.
Customer type priceA product price that applies to a specific customer group.
FulfillmentThe process of preparing, dispatching and delivering an order.
Soft deleteA record marked deleted but retained for possible restore/audit.
